MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

Not undoable. | 26:| No modifier | Places the whole file as a clip at the drop point. Nothing else moves. The drop is refused if the clip would overlap its neighbours in a way the overlap rule forbids. | Add Clip | 44:- **Refused drops spring back.** If the drop breaks the overlap rule (see [Limits](#limits)), the clip animates back to where it was and nothing changes. While you drag, positions the project refuses are skipped, and the clip stays at the last allowed position. 51:`,` and `.` move the selection one frame earlier or later. With ⇧ they move it ten frames. A nudge is an ordinary move, so the overlap rule can refuse it (undo name "Nudge Clips"). 85:*Agents:* `slip` takes `clip` and `delta`. `roll` takes `clip` (the clip to the right of the cut) and `to`. A roll is refused with "no clip on track … ends where clip … begins" when the clips don't touch. 132:A gap closes completely or not at all. A selection of several clips keeps its internal timing. The duplicate is refused if the copies would break the overlap rule. To place copies somewhere else, ⌥-drag instead (see [Moving clips](#moving-clips)). 163:**Paste** keeps the copied arrangement. The earliest clip lands at the playhead and the others keep their distance from it. The copied front-most lane goes onto the front track, the lanes behind it onto the tracks behind, and tracks are added at the back if there aren't enough. A pasted clip that would break the overlap rule goes on a new track at the front, so a paste is never refused for lack of room. You can paste into another project. Pasted clips get new identities and are snapped to the project's frame rate. 184:Each clip that can't be detached is refused with a reason: "clip … has no audio to detach: it is not a media clip", "…: media … has no audio track", or "…: its audio is switched off". 237:Some limits count the whole project even while you edit inside a nest: up to 4,096 clips and 64 tracks, and the eight-level nesting depth. Every edit tool takes an optional `scope`, a nest id, which applies the edit inside that nest using the nest's own ids and times. 13:- **Media and project settings.** Adding, relinking or removing media and changing the Document tab still work with a nest open. They change the whole project.
447:nest to reach those clips). See [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md).
35:With an In–Out range set on the timeline (Mark ▸ Set In and Set Out), **File ▸ New Project from Range…** opens a new project holding exactly that range, moved to start at 0. A clip across the range's In or Out is cut there, as **Split** cuts it; a transition across an edge becomes a hard start or end; markers inside the range are kept. Media that no kept clip plays are left out. The item is off with no range set, while a nest is open, and while a sheet is on the window.
45:It does not copy media files (the new project uses the same files), speed-ramp, isolated-voice or voice-effect renders (they are made again when needed), or a graphic's kept history. If the range cannot be kept — a nest clip across an edge, or nothing playing in it — the item beeps and shows why at the foot of the inspector.
202:- **The find band:** a **Search by name** field that filters as you type, ignoring case and accents ("resume" finds "Résumé.mov"; Esc clears it), a **Sort** popup (**Import Order**, Name, Duration, Kind), and an **Unused only** checkbox that shows only files no clip uses. Every sort is ascending, and files that tie stay in import order. A file used only inside a nest counts as used. None of these is saved with the project. If nothing matches: "No media matches the search or the filter." If the search or Unused only hides the selected row, that row is deselected.
230:- **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** / **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead** place the selected row at the playhead. They have no shortcut, and they are off until a row (not a LUT) is selected on the Media tab. The track is the selected clip's track, or the front track when no clip is selected. With a nest open, that is a track inside the nest.
246:| **Reveal in Timeline** | Selects every clip on the timeline that shows this file and scrolls to the earliest one; the inspector switches to the Clip tab. Off when nothing on the timeline uses the file, including when its only clips are inside a nest. For a LUT, it selects the clips whose look it is. |
255:- For footage: "Remove "*name*"? It is used by 3 clips, which will be removed with it." **Remove and Delete Clips** removes the file and those clips, including any inside nests, as one undo step.
302:- A project holds at most 4,096 clips and 64 tracks (counting those inside nests), 1,024 markers and 1,024 media files, with nests up to 8 deep.
